note: npm audit --json, run from the repo root (one npm-workspaces tree spanning backend and frontend): 8 vulnerable package names, all severity 'high' (npm audit's own metadata.vulnerabilities confirms: high 8, everything else 0). ONE ROOT CAUSE for all 8: multer@2.2.0, pulled in by @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3's EXACT pin (confirmed: `npm view @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 dependencies.multer` prints "2.2.0", no range operator). multer's own npm-audit entry lists FOUR published advisories: GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm (DoS via crafted multipart field names, high), GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf (DoS via a file-descriptor leak on aborted uploads, high), GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 (DoS via an oversized array index in field names, high), and GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (a file-size-limit bypass via an async fileFilter race condition, low) — all four are fixed together in multer 2.3.0. The other 7 names (@nestjs/core, @nestjs/platform-express, @nestjs/schedule, @nestjs/terminus, @nestjs/testing, @nestjs/typeorm, nestjs-pino) carry no advisory of their own; npm audit lists each only because it depends, directly or transitively, on the vulnerable multer. This app genuinely exercises the vulnerable code: it accepts image uploads up to 10 MB through multer via @nestjs/platform-express's FileInterceptor (backend/src/media, per root CLAUDE.md) — a live, reachable path, not a theoretical one. A clean fix was attempted and does NOT take: a root-level `overrides.multer: "^2.3.0"` entry was added, `npm install` and then `npm install --package-lock-only` were both run, and the lockfile still resolved multer to 2.2.0 both times, because npm's simple (non-nested) override form does not out-rank a direct parent's EXACT version pin — only the nested per-parent override form would, and that ships a version its parent (@nestjs/platform-express) never declared compatible, which is a repository-owner risk decision, not this verification task's call (RULING R18). The override attempt was fully reverted; this worktree carries no override and no dependency version change. Per R18, a production-tree, non-critical advisory (all 8 here are 'high', none 'critical') is RECORDED rather than blocked outright, but its entry must carry a `productionRisk` object with three independently non-stub fields (`vulnerability`, `reachability`, `fix` — see scripts/verify/checks/audit.mjs's header and `productionRiskProblems()`); a vague or missing one fails this check exactly as hard as an unrecorded advisory. This ratchet stays two-directional: a new advisory not listed here fails scripts/verify/checks/audit.mjs, and a listed entry npm audit no longer reports fails it too. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-15 on main's merged tree: npm audit now reports SIX vulnerable package names, not eight. @nestjs/schedule and nestjs-pino were deleted from this baseline on that date by this ratchet's own stale-entry rule, and the deletion is worth reading carefully, because NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CHANGED to earn it: both packages sit at the identical versions the merge-base lockfile pinned (@nestjs/schedule 12.0.1, nestjs-pino 5.1.0, verified against `git show <merge-base>:package-lock.json`), both still peer-depend on @nestjs/core, and multer@2.2.0 is still pinned exactly where it was. What changed is npm audit's own cascade over an advisory database this repository does not control — the property this row's blindSpot names and the reason it lives in the full tier behind the npm-registry precondition rather than in the fast one. The six that remain (multer plus the five @nestjs/* names downstream of it) still trace to the same unfixed root cause, and their productionRisk records still stand unchanged: this is a narrower REPORT, not a smaller risk.

entries.name: multer
entries.reason: Root cause of all 8 entries in this baseline: four published DoS/bypass advisories in multer@2.2.0 itself. Fix exists (multer 2.3.0) but is blocked by @nestjs/platform-express's exact version pin — see productionRisk for full detail; this is not fixed in this task, only recorded, pending an owner decision.

productionRisk.vulnerability: multer@2.2.0 (pulled in by @nestjs/platform-express) carries four published GHSA advisories directly in its own npm-audit `via` list: GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm (Denial of Service via crafted multipart field names, high), GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf (Denial of Service via a file-descriptor leak on aborted uploads, high), GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 (Denial of Service via an oversized array index in field names, high), and GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (a file-size-limit bypass via an async fileFilter race condition, low). npm audit's own severity roll-up for the multer package name is 'high', driven by the three high-severity ones. All four are fixed together in multer 2.3.0.
productionRisk.reachability: Reachable: this app accepts image uploads up to 10 MB through multer via @nestjs/platform-express's FileInterceptor (backend/src/media; the 10 MB cap is documented in root CLAUDE.md's deployment section). This is a live, exercised code path in this application, not a theoretical advisory in an unused dependency.
productionRisk.fix: Fixed upstream in multer@2.3.0, but @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 (the latest 11.x release — the next is the major 12.0.0) pins multer to the EXACT string "2.2.0", not a range (confirmed: `npm view @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 dependencies.multer`). A root-level `overrides.multer: "^2.3.0"` entry was tried and does not take: after adding it and running `npm install` then `npm install --package-lock-only`, the lockfile still resolved multer to 2.2.0 both times — npm's simple override form does not out-rank a direct parent's exact pin; only the nested per-parent override form would, and that would ship a version @nestjs/platform-express never declared compatible with. That is a repository-owner risk decision (nested override, a NestJS v12 upgrade, or a formally accepted risk), not this verification task's call — recorded here, not fixed.

entries.name: @nestjs/core
entries.reason: Carries no advisory of its own — flagged only because it depends on the vulnerable @nestjs/platform-express, which depends on multer@2.2.0. Root cause and fix status are multer's; see productionRisk.

productionRisk.vulnerability: @nestjs/core has no advisory of its own; npm audit's `via` for this name is the bare package-name string "@nestjs/platform-express" (no titled advisory object). The real vulnerability is three hops away: multer@2.2.0's own DoS/bypass advisories GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 and GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (full detail in this baseline's `multer` entry), reached via @nestjs/core -> @nestjs/platform-express -> multer.
productionRisk.reachability: @nestjs/core itself sits on every request (it is this app's DI/bootstrap root) but exposes no vulnerable surface of its own. The actual reachable vulnerable code is multer's multipart parsing on this app's image-upload path (backend/src/media, up to 10 MB uploads) — described fully in the multer entry.
productionRisk.fix: No independent fix applies to @nestjs/core; it clears from npm audit's report the moment multer does. See the multer entry: fixed upstream in multer 2.3.0, blocked here because @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 pins multer to the exact version 2.2.0 and a root `overrides.multer` entry was tested (`npm install`, then `npm install --package-lock-only`) and does not override that exact pin. Recorded pending an owner decision (nested override, NestJS v12 upgrade, or an accepted-risk record).

entries.name: @nestjs/platform-express
entries.reason: The direct parent of the vulnerable multer@2.2.0 — carries no advisory of its own but is the package whose exact version pin blocks the fix. See productionRisk.

productionRisk.vulnerability: @nestjs/platform-express has no advisory of its own; npm audit's `via` for this name lists the bare package-name strings "@nestjs/core" and "multer" (no titled advisory object here — the titled advisories live on multer's own entry). The real vulnerability is multer@2.2.0's four DoS/bypass advisories GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 and GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (full detail in this baseline's `multer` entry) — @nestjs/platform-express is multer's DIRECT parent, one hop from the real vulnerability.
productionRisk.reachability: Reachable: @nestjs/platform-express wires multer's FileInterceptor into this app's image-upload path (backend/src/media, up to 10 MB uploads per root CLAUDE.md) — the same live path the multer entry describes, one hop closer to it than @nestjs/core.
productionRisk.fix: Same underlying fix as multer's entry: fixed upstream in multer 2.3.0, blocked because THIS package (@nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3, the latest 11.x release) pins multer to the exact string "2.2.0", not a range (confirmed via `npm view @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 dependencies.multer`). A root `overrides.multer: "^2.3.0"` entry was tested (`npm install`, then `npm install --package-lock-only`) and does not override an exact pin from a direct parent — only the nested per-parent override form would, shipping a multer version this package never declared compatible with, which is an owner decision. Recorded pending that decision (nested override, a NestJS v12 upgrade, or an accepted-risk record).

entries.reason: Cascades from multer@2.2.0's DoS advisories (GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4, GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72) purely through its @nestjs/core -> @nestjs/platform-express dependency chain; npm audit lists it with no advisory of its own, only package-name 'via' entries.
